chunks: Zurarah narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام that he said:
“Nothing of the adhān suffices for you except what you make yourself hear or understand, and articulate the alif and the hāʾ clearly.

And send blessings upon the Prophet and his family, may the blessings of Allah be upon them, whenever you mention him or a mentioner mentions him in your presence, whether in the adhān or other than it. And the stronger your voice is, without overstraining yourself, the more those who hear will be, and your reward in that will be greater.”

key_terms.آلِهِ: his family, included in the salawat
key_terms.أَجْرُكَ: your reward from Allah for this act
key_terms.أَسْمَعْتَ: made to hear, meaning audible to oneself
key_terms.النَّبِيِّ: the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, upon whom blessings are to be sent
key_terms.الْأَذَانِ: the call to prayer being discussed in its proper recitation and etiquette
key_terms.صَوْتُكَ: your voice in calling the adhān
key_terms.فَهِمْتَهُ: understood it, referring to conscious and intelligible recitation

ai.seo_question: What are the etiquettes and legal requirements of pronouncing the adhān according to Imam al-Bāqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the adhān must be pronounced in a way that the caller himself can hear or comprehend, and that its letters should be articulated clearly. It also instructs sending blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family whenever he is mentioned, and encourages raising the voice in the adhān moderately so that more people hear it and the reward increases.
